summary: A Gaussian location-scale mixture g with M=E[T^(-1/2)] has Var(g)<=sqrt(2/pi) M. Under the checked full-matrix Gaussian-mixture theorem's normalized condition M<=sqrt(2*pi), every such marginal and every weak limit has total variation <=2. The admissible cap-one N-fragment indicator f_{N,L} has Var=2N, so any weak Gaussian-mixture approximation requires liminf M>=N sqrt(2*pi); an unbounded-support countable-fragment example has infinite variation. Quantitatively, any cap-one probability density g with Var(g)<=V obeys ||f_{N,L}-g||_1 >= (2N-V)/(N+1/L). This refutes only a constant-preserving per-coordinate Gaussian-mixture localization of arbitrary rough laws, not QFORM. The account04/B14 physical-triple theorem still gives ||p_Q||_infty<=6 sqrt(pi) for Q=X^T B_* X with B_*=I-(2/3)11^T and these fragmented inputs.
scope: Intermediate localization route only. No QFORM counterexample; full conjecture and full-target continuity remain open.
